title: FLAKE: test_status_shows_the_plan_gate fails intermittently in full-suite runs (TR-068 recurrence, no root cause)
description:
tests/test_quota_gate.py::test_status_shows_the_plan_gate fails ONCE in a while in a full-suite run and passes standalone. Observed again 2026-09-20 in a 579-test run (578 passed, 1 failed) at commit 9eba6a6; a rerun of the full suite immediately after was 579/579 green, and the test passes standalone every time.

The test ALREADY carries a TR-068 note saying it "failed ONCE in a loaded 453-test run and has not reproduced in 99 executions since". So this is a RECURRENCE of a known fixture, not a new break, and the TR-068 dump did its job (the failure is captured with gated/expired/stdout). What is still missing is the ROOT CAUSE.

Current shape: the test writes a quota-state.json into tmp_path, sets ROUTER_STATE_DIR + ROUTING_REGISTRY, and shells out to router_status.py twice (json then text) asserting "plan-gate zai-glm GATED until" appears. The assertion that failed is the reset_at equality (line 593), i.e. the CLASSIFICATION, not the rendering — the gate for zai-glm was not seen as gated in that run.

Hypotheses to test, in order:
  1. A sibling test in the same session writes a real quota-state.json or mutates a shared registry/resolver cache that router_status.py picks up when the two subprocess invocations interleave. Check for tests that do NOT set ROUTER_STATE_DIR and for any module-level cache in the gate classifier.
  2. Timing: the expiry classification compares against "now" — a gate whose reset_at sits close to a boundary could flip between the two subprocess runs under load. _utc(5) is 5 minutes out, so a boundary flip needs a 5-minute stall; measure the real gap between the two runs.
  3. subprocess env leakage: env=dict(os.environ, ...) inherits the parent process env; if an earlier test exported ROUTER_STATE_DIR or a ROUTER_* variable into os.environ, the child could see both.

ACCEPTANCE: the flake is explained by a named mechanism (not "load"), the mechanism is pinned by a test that fails deterministically without the fix, and 3 consecutive full-suite runs are green.

RESOLVED 2026-09-20 (db66d4d) — root cause found and proven, guard added.

ROOT CAUSE: `_utc()` has SECOND resolution. The test computed `_utc(5)` TWICE — once to write the state file, once inside the assertion — and compared the two strings for equality, with TWO SUBPROCESS LAUNCHES between the calls. Any second boundary falling in that gap fails the comparison. A coin flip that widens under load = exactly the observed signature (fails in a loaded full-suite run, always passes standalone, never reproducible on demand). The product was never at fault; the assertion re-derived its own expected value.

PROOF (deterministic, no load required): write a stamp, sleep 1.1s as the stand-in for the two subprocess launches, recompute -> the strings differ. Hypothesis 2 in this row was the right one; hypotheses 1 and 3 (sibling state leak, env leakage) are RULED OUT — the failure needs only elapsed time.

FIX: capture the stamp once and reuse it.

GUARD: test_no_test_recomputes_a_timestamp_it_compares_for_equality scans the whole suite for a time helper CALLED inside a comparison. Verified RED-on-bug / GREEN-on-fix by reintroducing the exact line in the real file — the guard names it (test_quota_gate.py:604). A second test pins that the second-resolution window is real, so the reasoning behind the guard is itself checked.

SIDE FINDING: `pytest-randomly` is NOT installed in the board venv, so collection order is fixed and no seed sweep is possible — recorded so a future investigation does not burn a cycle retrying it.

title: [P1] BUILD: task-router proxy — speak the real Hermes gateway session protocol (/v1/responses SSE passthrough, X-Hermes-Session-Key/Id, idle timeouts)

SOURCE A - the scheduler's own gateway client, i.e. the exact calls the fleet already makes to Hermes (coding-hermes-scheduler/internal/scheduler/gateway_stream.go + gateway_client.go): POST {gateway}/v1/responses body: {"input": "", "model": "", "provider": "

", "require_approval": false, "stream": true} headers: Content-Type: application/json; X-Hermes-Session-Key: ; auth reads back X-Hermes-Session-Id FROM THE RESPONSE HEADERS at stream open (that is the real gateway session id, more precise than the resp_* envelope id) parses SSE: "event:" / "data:" lines, JSON with a "type" field; terminal events are "response.completed" / "response.failed" TIME BUDGET: an IDLE deadline, not a wall clock (SCHED-GAP-119). turnWatch.notify() resets the timer on every real SSE event; the request is cancelled only when the gap between events exceeds the deadline. A wall clock exists only as the outer bound. SOURCE B - the Hermes API contract (hermes-agent website docs, api-server.md): - ALL SSE streams emit a ": keepalive" comment line every 10s when idle, explicitly "so long tool calls do not trip client idle timeouts". Parsers MUST skip ":" lines. - X-Hermes-Session-Key: stable per-channel identifier for long-term memory, INDEPENDENT of the transcript-scoped X-Hermes-Session-Id (which rotates on /new). <=256 chars, control chars rejected, ECHOED BACK on responses (JSON + SSE), advertised in /v1/capabilities as "session_key_header". - Responses streams emit spec-native function_call / function_call_output output items; Chat Completions emits event: hermes.tool.progress. - Idle sessions release their memory provider after agent.agent_cache.idle_ttl_secs (default 1h). - The gateway also advertises /v1/capabilities, /v1/toolsets, /v1/skills, /v1/runs and /v1/runs/{id}/events. THE GAP. Our proxy front door (scripts/router_server.py, PROXY_PATHS = ("/v1/chat/completions", "/v1/responses")) was built against a BUFFERED JSON mirror: - stream:true is STRIPPED and the buffered answer is re-served as synthesized SSE, so keepalives, hermes.tool.progress and function_call items never reach the client; - X-Hermes-Session-Key is not forwarded inward and not echoed back; X-Hermes-Session-Id from upstream is discarded, and the ledger row carries a synthetic per-call id (router-proxy-) - the TR-122 defect; - the hop budget is a FIXED 180s WALL (ROUTER_PROXY_HOP_TIMEOUT_S), which kills exactly the long agent sessions the scheduler runs (observed 2026-09-24: a hard refactor prompt through the proxy outlived 300s and had to be re-run in the background); - non-OpenAI advertised endpoints (capabilities/toolsets/skills/runs*) are not passed through, so a probing harness falls back - the same failure class as the /v1/models 404 fixed in d181884. WHY THIS MATTERS NOW. The scheduler routes foremen through this shape, so until the proxy speaks it, "point the router at Hermes" means degrading a streaming session protocol into one blocking JSON call per turn. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (all must be proven with recorded evidence, not asserted): 1. STREAM PASSTHROUGH: client stream:true => upstream SSE forwarded unmodified, including ": keepalive" comment lines, hermes.tool.progress, and function_call / function_call_output items, in order. Prove with a captured transcript showing >=1 keepalive line during an idle gap and tool events in order. 2. SESSION CONTINUITY: X-Hermes-Session-Key forwarded inward AND echoed back; upstream X-Hermes-Session-Id surfaced to the client; the ledger row (data/state/outcomes.jsonl) records the REAL session id. Prove across >=2 turns of one logical session that the id is stable and that Hermes sees one session, not two. 3. IDLE TIMEOUTS, NOT WALL: replace the fixed 180s wall with an idle deadline reset by every upstream event/byte (keepalive counts as activity) plus a generous outer cap (default ~2h, env-overridable). Bound everything by env knobs, keep the 0=off escape. Prove: a stream that goes quiet ~30s mid-tool-call SURVIVES; a stream that emits nothing for the idle window is aborted with a distinct logged reason (never a silent hang, never a garbage 200). 4. SURFACE PASSTHROUGH: /v1/capabilities, /v1/toolsets, /v1/skills and /v1/runs* are proxied (read-through) so a harness probing them does not fall back to a direct lane. 5. COMPLEXITY + EXECUTION LOG PROOF: the response and the ledger row together must show complexity_source, the requirements matrix, complexity_sig, the served model+provider, steps/tokens, and - joined to state.db - that the agent actually executed (tool calls), so an operator can prove "this prompt scored X and model Y ran it". 6. NO REGRESSION: full suite green at HEAD; the four existing failure-policy invariants (transient 429 must not block boot; non-JSON upstream must advance the ladder; a plan lane stamped 0 must never read FREE; unmeasured stays None) stay pinned. DEPLOY NOTE: the live install ~/.hermes/scripts/router_server.py is a SYMLINK into this repo, so a pull is not a deploy - run scripts/sync_runtime.sh and RESTART task-router-proxy (:9391) and task-router-server (:9092), then prove the change is live (commit hash in /health + a real streamed call). Long runs are expected here: use idle-based budgets, do not add wall-clock shortcuts, and do not shorten a run to make it fit a timeout - the source runs are minutes-long agent sessions by design. OPERATOR CONTRACT CLARIFICATION (Bane, 2026-09-24 - this is the shape to build). The router is the MIDDLE LAYER: the scheduler's Hermes calls come to US instead of straight to the gateway, and this is the required flow: 1. INGEST the scheduler's own call shape (the one SOURCE A documents): POST /v1/responses with X-Hermes-Session-Key, stream:true, require_approval:false. It must be a DROP-IN: pointing the scheduler's gateway base URL at the router must require NO scheduler code change. Every hop we make upstream is a normal Hermes gateway call, so the gateway stays the execution engine - we are the routing layer, not a replacement. 2. RATE the incoming prompt: the LLM/classifier returns complexity BY CATEGORY for that specific prompt (not a fixed profile). No task text, no rating - fail-open with a visible degraded marker, never a silent fixed list. 3. FIND the chain options in the task database (registry tables) for those requirements. 4. CALL Hermes IN CHAIN ORDER, walking the fallback ladder as needed when a hop fails or is gated, and keep going until an answer is served or the chain is exhausted (with a self-auditing ladder trail - an exhausted chain must be explainable hop by hop). 5. LET IT RUN. These are long agent sessions (minutes to hours). Budget with IDLE timeouts, never a wall clock: reset on every upstream event/byte (the 10s ': keepalive' counts as activity), with a generous outer cap and an env kill switch. A hop that is working must never be cut off for being slow; a hop that has gone silent must be abandoned with a distinct logged reason. 6. RETURN THE STATS WITH THE ANSWER.
